'''Christian James McCollum''' (born September 19, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball|Lehigh Mountain Hawks]] and was named the [[Patriot League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Patriot League Player of the Year]] in 2010 and 2012. McCollum was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] tenth overall in the [[2013 NBA draft]]. He was chosen as the [[NBA Most Improved Player]] in 2016. McCollum was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in 2022, the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2025, and to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in 2026. McCollum served as president of the [[National Basketball Players Association]] from 2021 to 2025.

==High school career==
McCollum played high school basketball for the Golden Eagles at [[GlenOak High School]] in his native city of [[Canton, Ohio]]. As a freshman in 2005, he was considerably undersized, standing at only {{Height|ft=5|in=2|out=unit}}. Despite his stature, McCollum played varsity as a freshman for the Golden Eagles, relying on his athleticism.<ref name="Desire">{{cite news |first=Joe |last=Freeman |title=McCollum's Desire is Just the Right Size: The Once-Slender Guard Has Blossomed into a Hard-Working Playmaker |newspaper=The Oregonian |date=July 9, 2013 |pages=D1, D4}}</ref> McCollum would eventually benefit from a late growth spurt, gaining five inches by his second year and another four inches by his third year of high school; it proved enough to put him on the radar for college recruitment.<ref name="Desire"/> In his very first game as a junior, McCollum came away with 54 points to set both school and Stark County records.<ref name="Desire"/>

Throughout his high school career, McCollum worked at refining his shooting stroke; the successful effort was reflected in the 29.3 points per game he averaged during his senior season.<ref name="Desire"/> By graduation, McCollum had become the leading scorer in Golden Eagles history, with 1,405 career points, and was named [[Gatorade]] Ohio Player of the Year for his final campaign, the 2008–09 season.<ref name="Desire"/>

==College career==
[[File:C. J. McCollum at Lehigh.jpg|thumb|left|McCollum playing for Lehigh in 2012]]
McCollum played at the private research school [[Lehigh University]] for four seasons. Listed at {{Height|ft=6|in=3|out=unit}} and {{Convert|165|lb|kg|abbr=unit}} as a [[2009–10 Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball team|freshman in 2009–10]], he made an immediate impact for the [[Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball|Mountain Hawks]].<ref name=Desire/> He played in 33 games, starting in 31, and averaged 19.1 points and 5 rebounds per game while shooting 45.9 percent from the field.<ref name=BIO/> He was the leading freshman scorer in the nation and the first player in [[Patriot League]] history to be named conference [[Patriot League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Player]] and Rookie of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.patriotleague.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030110aaa.html |title=Patriot League Men's Basketball All-League Teams and Awards Announced |access-date=November 14, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727170029/http://www.patriotleague.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030110aaa.html |archive-date=July 27, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Also, he was an [[Associated Press]] honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]. McCollum led the Mountain Hawks to the [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2010 NCAA tournament]], where he put up 26 points in a first-round loss to a top-seeded [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] team.<ref name=BIO>{{cite web |url=http://www.lehighsports.com/sports/mbball/rosters/displayplayer.aspx?playerid=8006 |title=Lehigh athletics biography |access-date=November 14, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319203459/http://www.lehighsports.com/sports/mbball/rosters/displayplayer.aspx?playerid=8006 |archive-date=March 19, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2010–11, McCollum increased his averages to 21.8 points and 7.8 rebounds per outing. He played and started in 31 contests and shot 39.9 percent from the field. His shooting percentages dipped to 39.9 percent from the field, as did Lehigh's record, and McCollum was edged out for conference Player of the Year honors by [[Mike Muscala]] of the [[Bucknell Bison men's basketball|Bucknell Bisons]]. McCollum was named First Team All-Conference.<ref name=BIO/>

As a junior in the [[2011–12 Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball team|2011–12]] campaign, McCollum again earned Patriot League Player of the Year, as well as his third straight First Team All-Conference designation.<ref>{{cite web |title=2011–12 Men's Basketball All-Patriot League Teams and Major Awards Announced |publisher=[[Patriot League]] |date=February 27, 2012 |url=http://www.patriotleague.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022712aaa.html |format=Press release |access-date=February 27, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202105335/http://www.patriotleague.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022712aaa.html |archive-date=February 2, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2012, the Mountain Hawks beat the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], 75–70, in the school's first ever victory at the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Division I tournament]], during which McCollum posted a game-high 30 points; this marked only the sixth time in the history of the tournament that a team seeded 15th defeated a team seeded second.<ref name="morningcall">{{cite news |url=http://www.mcall.com/sports/college/lehigh/mc-ncaa-basketball-lehigh-duke-gamer-0316-20120316,0,6364456.story |title=NCAA basketball: Lehigh pulls off monumental upset of Duke |newspaper=The Morning Call |date=March 16, 2012 |last=Housenick |first=Tom |access-date=March 16, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140310044820/http://articles.mcall.com/2012-03-16/sports/mc-ncaa-basketball-lehigh-duke-gamer-0316-20120316_1_mccollum-3-pointer-gabe-knutson-lehigh |archive-date=March 10, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Over his four college years, McCollum added 30 pounds of muscle to fill out his frame.<ref name=Desire/> Even though he was already considered virtually destined to be a top NBA draft pick by his third year, he decided to finish his final year of college instead of leaving sooner for the NBA. A journalism major, McCollum penned an article for ''[[Sporting News]]'' explaining why he opted to continue on with his education.<ref>{{cite web|title=C.J. McCollum: Why I'm returning to Lehigh for my senior year|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball-news/2178868-cj-mccollum-lehigh-nba-draft-staying|work=SportingNews.com|date=April 9, 2012|access-date=May 26, 2016|archive-date=June 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160625072619/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball-news/2178868-cj-mccollum-lehigh-nba-draft-staying|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On November 25, 2012, McCollum scored 26 points in a 91–77 win over [[Sacred Heart Pioneers men's basketball|Sacred Heart]] to pass [[Rob Feaster]] as the Patriot League's all-time leading scorer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=McCollum breaks record in 91–77 win at Sacred Heart |publisher=[[Lehigh University]] |date=November 25, 2012 |url=http://www.lehighsports.com/sports/mbball/mccollum_breaks_record_in_91-77_win_at_sacred_heart.aspx |access-date=November 26, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121210212014/http://www.lehighsports.com/sports/mbball/mccollum_breaks_record_in_91-77_win_at_sacred_heart.aspx |archive-date=December 10, 2012 }}</ref> On January 5, 2013, McCollum broke his left foot in a game against the [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU Rams]], ending his season early. He was a 2012–13 [[List of Senior CLASS Award men's basketball winners|Senior CLASS Award]] finalist.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020613aad.html |title=Hulls Named Finalist for Senior CLASS Award |date=February 6, 2013 |publisher=IUHoosiers.com |access-date=February 13, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130215113340/http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020613aad.html |archive-date=February 15, 2013 }}</ref> McCollum went on to graduate from Lehigh University with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in [[Journalism]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://lehighsports.com/news/2016/4/22/mens-basketball-lehigh-alum-c-j-mccollum-named-kia-nba-most-improved-player.aspx|title=Lehigh alum C.J. McCollum named Kia NBA Most Improved Player|website=Lehigh University Athletics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www2.lehigh.edu/news/cj-mccollum-more-than-just-a-basketball-player|title=C.J. McCollum: 'More than just a basketball player'|website=Lehigh University}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Portland Trail Blazers (2013–2022)===

====2013–2015: Early years====
[[File:McCollum-CJ-150105.jpg|thumb|right|McCollum with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in 2015]]
The first player to ever enter the NBA from Lehigh, McCollum was picked tenth overall in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He signed his rookie scale contract with the franchise on July 11,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2013/07/trail_blazers_sign_rookie_cj_mccollum.html|title=Trail Blazers sign rookie CJ McCollum|work=OregonLive.com|date=July 11, 2013|access-date=July 11, 2013}}</ref> and he proceeded to play for them in the [[2013 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]], averaging 21 points and 4 rebounds per game.

Having convened for an annual photoshoot, the rookie class of 2013 took an NBA.com survey, according to which McCollum was voted the 2013–14 Rookie of the Year (together with [[Victor Oladipo]]).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/features/john_schuhmann/08/26/2013-14-nba-rookie-survey/index.html |title=Magic's Oladipo among rookie favorites to stand out in 2013–14 |date=August 26, 2013 |last=Schuhmann |first=John |work=NBA.com |access-date=October 15, 2013}}</ref> McCollum sat out the first six weeks of the regular season with a foot injury. On January 1, 2014, he was assigned to the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the development league.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15003|title=Trail Blazers assign CJ McCollum to D-League|work=InsideHoops.com|date=January 1, 2014|access-date=January 1, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102193856/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15003|archive-date=January 2, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was recalled by the Blazers on January 5 and made his NBA debut three days later, during which he notched 4 points as Portland beat the [[Orlando Magic]], 110–94.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140108/ORLPOR/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Blazers 110, Magic 94 |work=NBA.com |date=January 8, 2014 |access-date=January 8, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140108010632/http://www.nba.com/games/20140108/ORLPOR/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 8, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On February 8, McCollum posted a season-high 19 points in a 117–110 victory over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mccolcj01/gamelog/2014/ |title=C.J. McCollum 2013–14 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=December 27, 2015}}</ref>

On October 27, 2014, Portland exercised its third-year team option to extend McCollum's rookie scale contract through 2015–16.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-exercise-team-options-meyers-leonard-and-cj-mccollum|title=Trail Blazers Exercise Team Options On Meyers Leonard And CJ McCollum|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 27, 2014|access-date=October 27, 2014}}</ref> For his sophomore season, he played 15.7 minutes per outing while averaging 6.8 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 1 assist across 62 games.<ref name="bball">{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mccolcj01.html|title=CJ McCollum Stats|work=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]|access-date=November 27, 2019}}</ref> During a first-round playoff loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], Game 5, McCollum scored a then career high of 33 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150429/PORMEM/gameinfo.html|title=Grizzlies advance, beating Trail Blazers 99–93 in Game 5|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=April 29, 2015|access-date=September 30, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015061559/http://www.nba.com/games/20150429/PORMEM/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 15, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2015–2016: Most Improved Player====
Exercising their fourth-year team option on September 30, 2015, the Trail Blazers extended McCollum's rookie scale contract through the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-exercise-team-options-mccollum-plumlee-and-vonleh|title=Trail Blazers Exercise Team Options On McCollum, Plumlee and Vonleh|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=September 30, 2015|access-date=September 30, 2015}}</ref> With four of Portland's previous starters—[[LaMarcus Aldridge]], [[Nicolas Batum]], [[Wesley Matthews]], and [[Robin Lopez]]—having departed, only star point guard [[Damian Lillard]] remained; thus McCollum was elevated to starting shooting guard to join Lillard in the backcourt for the 2015–16 campaign. As such, he saw his minutes increase to 34.8 per contest, and he started in all 80 games that he played. For the season, he would average 20.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 4.3 assists a night across 80 games.<ref name="bball"/> In the season-opener on October 28, McCollum posted a career-high 37 points, scoring 22 of which in the first quarter alone, helping the Blazers defeat the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], 112–94.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NOPPOR/gameinfo.html|title=McCollum scores 37 as Blazers down Pelicans 112–94|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180507024227/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NOPPOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 7, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> After injury decommissioned Lillard in late December, McCollum filled in as the primary point guard. ==Broadcasting career==
McCollum hosts a weekly podcast, ''Pull Up with CJ McCollum'', that is produced by [[Cadence13]].<ref name="Mickanen">{{cite news |last=Mickanen |first=Dylan |title=CJ McCollum in favor of playing out the rest of the season at a single site |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/portland-trail-blazers/cj-mccollum-reveals-his-previous-5-jobs |access-date=April 17, 2020 |publisher=Northwest Sports |date=April 16, 2020 |archive-date=December 2, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201202191615/https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/portland-trail-blazers/cj-mccollum-reveals-his-previous-5-jobs |url-status=dead }}</ref> It is co-hosted by ESPN analyst Jordan Schultz. McCollum has a podcast studio in his home and brings portable recording equipment with him when he is out of town.<ref name="Cacciola">{{cite news |last=Cacciola |first=Scott |title=C.J. McCollum's 'Healthy Habits': Yoga, Wine and Podcasting |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/10/22/sports/basketball/cj-mcollum-portland-trail-blazers.html |access-date=April 17, 2020 |work=The New York Times |date=October 22, 2019}}</ref> Guests on the show have included [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Carmelo Anthony]].<ref name="Cacciola"/><ref name="Goldberg">{{cite news |last=Goldberg |first=Jamie |title=CJ McCollum reacts to NBA suspending season, remains hopeful that season will resume |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2020/03/cj-mccollum-reacts-to-nba-suspending-season-remains-hopeful-that-season-will-resume.html |access-date=April 17, 2020 |publisher=The Oregonian |date=March 13, 2020}}</ref> In a March 2020 episode of the podcast, McCollum was recording when he received news that the NBA was suspending the 2020 season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="Goldberg"/>

On May 30, 2022, McCollum signed a multiplatform deal with ESPN to be an NBA analyst.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34010728 |title=New Orleans Pelicans' CJ McCollum joining ESPN as an NBA analyst |work=ESPN |agency=Associated Press |date=May 30, 2022 |access-date=May 30, 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
McCollum has been married to his college sweetheart, Elise Esposito, since October 27, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=CJ McCollum and Elise Esposito's Wedding Was an Intimate Affair in Oregon Wine Country|url=https://www.vogue.com/slideshow/cj-mccollum-elise-esposito-oregon-wedding|date=January 6, 2021|access-date=September 15, 2022}}</ref> They have one son named Jacobi, who was born on January 10, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=CJ and Elise McCollum welcome son Jacobi James McCollum|url=https://www.kgw.com/article/news/local/cj-and-elise-mccollum-welcome-son/283-04b4e4ac-7527-4941-92ed-bc40da04b975|date=January 17, 2022|access-date=September 15, 2022|website=kgw.com}}</ref> McCollum's older brother, [[Errick McCollum|Errick]], is a [[EuroLeague]] winner professional basketball player. Off the court, McCollum has long taken a keen interest in [[journalism]]. As such, he has written articles concerning the NBA for various media outlets;<ref>{{cite web|title=C.J. McCollum: 'More Than Just a Basketball Player'|url=http://www1.lehigh.edu/news/cj-mccollum-more-just-basketball-player|date=June 27, 2013|access-date=April 30, 2015}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> in one of his pieces, he interviewed the [[Commissioner of the NBA|Commissioner]] of the league [[Adam Silver]].<ref>{{cite web|title=CJ Sits Down with the Commish|url=http://allball.blogs.nba.com/tag/c-j-mccollum/|publisher=NBA|date=July 9, 2014|access-date=April 30, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150419144212/http://allball.blogs.nba.com/tag/c-j-mccollum/|archive-date=April 19, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

McCollum is involved in his community as a radio personality and philanthropist. In 2016, he opened up the CJ McCollum Dream Center, which is an innovative learning room at the Blazers Boys & Girls Club outfitted with new computers, books, art, and learning tools. The Center aims to provide a safe and inspiring space for underserved youth to learn, explore, create, and grow.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 8, 2016 |title=CJ McCollum Dream Center Opens at Blazers Boys & Girls Club |url=http://bgcportland.org/blazers/dream-room/ |access-date=March 20, 2017 |website= Boys & Girls Clubs of Portland Metropolitan Area}}</ref> McCollum also helps foster local youths' interest in journalists through an initiative called CJ's Press Pass; it grants aspiring journalists access to postgame news conferences and provides them the opportunity to attend events with McCollum, to receive personalized mentorship from members of the media, and to have their work published.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Evans |first=Kelley D. |date=February 10, 2017 |title=Portland's CJ McCollum is a Silent Assassin on the Court and a Blooming Journalist Off of it |url=https://andscape.com/features/nba-portland-trail-blazer-cj-mccollum-journalist/ |access-date=March 20, 2017 |website=Andscape}}</ref>

McCollum is a wine enthusiast.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Davis|first=Scott|title=NBA star CJ McCollum is keeping his hotel room a frigid temperature to create a wine cellar for the 84 bottles he ordered to the Disney bubble|url=https://www.insider.com/cj-mccollum-wine-nba-bubble-2020-8|access-date=August 27, 2020|website=Insider|date=June 25, 2020 }}</ref> During the [[2020 NBA Bubble]], he brought 84 bottles in with him.<ref name=":0"/> He has his own label, McCollum Heritage 91, named after the street he grew up on and his birth year.<ref name=":0"/> In 2026, the label was rebranded to McCollum Family Vineyard.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-16 |title=Ex-Blazer CJ McCollum unveils new Oregon wine brand |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/portland/news/2026/06/16/cj-mccollum-family-vineyard-oregon-wine.html |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=Portland Business Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>
